column3: Close to the Hebrew.

Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names the soul and a rock in the singular; BSB says yourself and rocks.
The Hebrew names light and a spark; BSB says lamp and flame.
The Hebrew places the lamp above him; BSB says beside him.
The Hebrew has steps in the plural and counsel in the singular; BSB has stride and schemes.
The Hebrew says he was sent into a net, using the passive; BSB makes his feet the active subject.

The Hebrew explicitly names his feet; BSB says his every step.
The Hebrew calls his strength hungry; BSB says depleted.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew makes his confidence the subject of being torn from the tent; BSB makes him the subject.
The Hebrew does not explicitly name fire as the inhabitant; BSB supplies fire and describes burning sulfur raining down.
The Hebrew has a branch in the singular and describes its being cut off; BSB has branches withering.
The Hebrew places his name outside; BSB says in the land.
The Hebrew uses active plural verbs; BSB uses passive clauses.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly names his day; BSB says his fate.
The Hebrew has dwellings in the plural; BSB has dwelling.
